title: Iki entity type (iki/v1)
description: A kind of entity, such as a protein or a compound. Each type gets its own table, with history and per-field provenance.

name.description: The type's name in PascalCase. Elsewhere it is `plugin.Name`.

schema_version.description: Increase it whenever the fields change. Other plugins' dependencies and actions name the versions they work with.

extends.description: A parent type: entities of this type are also entities of the parent, with its fields.

abstract.description: Only subtypes have entities; nobody creates one of this type itself.

sample.description: Its records are samples, or material taken from them: a project's Files are found by the sample they belong to, the files its records hold and those a run that read one read or made. Its subtypes' records are samples too.

hrid.description: Human-readable IDs, such as PRT-000123. Never reused.

prefix.description: 2 to 8 capital letters or digits, starting with a letter.

digits.description: The number is padded with zeros to at least this many digits. Defaults to 6.

identity.description: The fields that make an entity the same as another: its registry entry's identity (ADR 0115). They must be the type's own, immutable, and at least one required: an optional one without a value is null in the identity (ADR 0104).

refines.description: For each list of rows this type inherits whose rows have roles by one of their fields (`by`): every role its rows may have, each with how many rows take it and what their references may refer to, within what its parent's say (ADR 0164). A specific complex says what its parts are this way.

roles.description: Per role: how many rows take it, and what their references may refer to. A row may have only these.

draws_received.description: An optional computed JSON field on a record, inherited by its subtypes. Iki appends each material draw into the record here, in the ledger transaction, so reviews sign the quantities and source revisions used.

draw_guards.description: Conditions on taking an amount, including transfers and splits. Each subtype also keeps its ancestors' guards. CEL reads record, now, today (midnight UTC), operation (draw, transfer, split) and purpose (routine or qa_sampling).

draw_purposes.description: The lab roles allowed to draw for each purpose in the record's project. Routine draws are open to Editors unless restricted. QA sampling requires a declaration. Subtypes inherit each purpose and may narrow its allowed roles.

by.description: One of these project lab roles is required in addition to permission to draw.

draw_target.description: Accept one ledger draw from the assigned record while in the designated state. A prepared draw also fixes the upstream source, quantity and authorized roles.

unit.description: An enum or string field holding the planned amount's UCUM unit, when the amount is a float rather than a quantity in one fixed unit.

due.description: A date or datetime field of the type (or a parent's) saying when its records are due: My work sorts what's assigned to someone by it, soonest first (ADR 0122).

notifications.description: Whom its records tell, and when (ADR 0129): on a state's change or a field's, the people its fields name, holders of a lab role in its project, its creator or its watchers, in Iki and by email. Each by name, which never changes once released: people's choices are kept by it.

request.description: Its records are requests a project sends to another project's service, such as a core facility (ADR 0132). The asking project owns each request; the service it's sent to may change only the fields named here, and set only the state fields named here, while the rest stay the asking project's. Its subtypes are requests too; a subtype may declare `request` with only `service_fields`, naming more of its own fields the service writes, such as a ranking a lab's core keeps (ADR 0232).

service_fields.description: The fields the service writes, such as its status, schedule and priority: state fields it sets with the lab roles its own people hold, and other fields its Editors change. They can't be references or files, required without a default, unique or immutable.

sends.description: References (or lists of them) whose records go to the service with the request, such as its samples: the service can read them, and only them, as long as the request is there.

completed.description: The service state that completes delivery. Each commissioned material needs a signed, returned result, and every recorded result must be signed and returned.

materials.description: Fields in sends that identify individual physical records. A result may cover those records and their recorded aliquots. A registry entry shared by several records cannot identify the tested material.

receives.description: What the service receives against the request (ADR 0180): a list of references it `sends`, to a type with `storage`, such as its tubes. The service checks each in with a receipt, as matched, missing, damaged or rejected, with what's extra.

by.description: The lab roles, held in the service's project, that receive them. Any Editor of the service, if none are named.

work_item.description: Its records are internal work for a request (ADR 0132). Only the service project creates and keeps them.

of.description: The name of the required, immutable reference to the request.

result.description: Its records are what a service makes for a request (ADR 0132): made in the service's project, which owns them, and sent back to the asking project once the service's own state field says it's released.

of.description: Its reference to the request it's a result of: a required, immutable `ref` to a request type.

material.description: An immutable reference to material covered by the request. It may be empty only when the request specifies no physical material.

released.description: The state field, and its states, in which it goes back to the asking project. It stays there after, as a correction shows in its state and history.

title.description: How an entity is named in lists and links, such as `{{ name or hrid }}`.

viewers.description: Iki's own viewers for its entities, each a tab on their pages, configured by naming the fields they show. Its subtypes' pages show them too, unless they declare their own.

exports.description: The files Iki writes of its records, offered on their pages and through the API at any revision, each download audited (ADR 0171). Configured by naming the fields each file is written from. Its subtypes have them too, unless they declare their own.

storage.description: Its records are kept somewhere, or keep others (ADR 0180): Iki keeps where each is, in which container and position, who has it, and every move, as a ledger of its own.

holds.description: The types (or their ancestors) of what can be kept in it, such as racks and boxes in a freezer, or tubes in a box.

grid.description: Its positions, in rows and columns: a box's, a rack's or a plate's. Each record it holds is at one of them, and no two at one.

rows.description: How many rows: a number (at most 32), or the name of one of its own required, immutable int fields.

columns.description: How many columns: a number (at most 48), or the name of one of its own required, immutable int fields.

labels.description: How its positions are named. `letter_number`: rows A, B, … and columns 1, 2, …, so A1 to H12; `number`: 1, 2, … in its order.

order.description: The order its positions are numbered and filled in: `by_row` (A1, A2, …) or `by_column` (A1, B1, …).

barcode.description: A unique string field holding the code on it already, such as a pre-barcoded tube's: what a scan reads and a label prints. Its HRID, if it has none.

label.description: A label's line under its title: text with `{{ }}` parts, as a display title has.

confirm.description: What needs its code scanned first, to confirm the record in someone's hand is the one they chose: a `draw` from its amount, or a `move`.

stock_catalogue.description: Maps a catalogue record to its lots, ledger unit, routine-use reorder threshold, open orders and project alert recipients (ADR 0190).

amount.description: How much of each record there is (ADR 0139): kept in `unit`, never below zero, and changed only by drawing, transferring, splitting into aliquots or adjusting it, each kept in its ledger.

label.description: What it's called, such as Volume. Defaults to Amount.

unit.description: The UCUM unit it's kept in: a volume, a mass, an amount of substance, or a count such as `{vial}`.

whole_units.description: Require whole quantities in the ledger unit for indivisible stock such as individual consumables. Applies after unit conversion.

display_unit.description: The unit people see it in, if not `unit`.

concentration.description: A quantity field of the type saying how much each unit of volume holds, so it can be drawn in a unit the concentration converts it to: 50 ug of a sample at 2 mg/mL is 25 uL.

material.description: An immutable reference naming what the amount is of, or id when this record is the material. A positive stock balance requires an identified material. A transfer into one of its records takes only the same entity's, and its aliquots are that entity's too.

follows.description: References whose records' eligibility a draw from it also meets (ADR 0180), such as a tube's lot: a state holding the source's amount holds its, and the source's draw guards are checked with the source as `record`. The first that's set is the draw's source, kept with its movement.

aliquots.description: What its aliquots are: records of another type, with a reference to the record each was split from. Its own type, by default.

type.description: The aliquots' type, which has an amount of its own.

of.description: That type's reference to the record each was split from.

export.description: What it writes. `sequence`: a DNA or RNA sequence, as GenBank (with its features) and as FASTA.

sequence.description: A string field with format `dna_sequence` or `rna_sequence`, whose `topology` and `strands` say its topology and strandedness; or a reference to a type that exports a sequence, whose file is written under this record's name with this record's features added.

features.description: A json field of features along it, as the sequence viewer reads them: each with a `type`, a `start` and `end` (from 1), and optionally a `name`, a `strand`, `parts` and `qualifiers`.

description.description: A string or text field describing it: GenBank's DEFINITION, and the FASTA header after its name.

accession.description: A string field holding the INSDC accession, with its version, of the record it came from, such as L09137.2.

organism.description: A reference to iki/core.Organism: the taxon it's from, written as GenBank's source feature.

export.description: What it writes. `protein`: a protein's residues, as FASTA, with its ID, name and description in its header (ADR 0229).

sequence.description: A string field with format `protein_sequence`: its residues, N- to C-terminus, in one-letter codes.

description.description: A string or text field describing it: the FASTA header after its name.

organism.description: A reference to iki/core.Organism: the taxon it's from, written as NCBI's `[organism=…]` modifier.

export.description: What it writes. `compound`: a compound's structure as an MDL Molfile, and many as an SDF with their fields as its data (ADR 0229).

structure.description: A text field holding its structure as an MDL Molfile (V2000, or V3000 where V2000 can't hold it), with its coordinates.

export.description: A JSON report and its carried electronic signatures, as HTML or JSON.

report.description: The JSON field holding the report.

review.description: The state field whose signed transitions issue the report.

issued.description: The signed locking states, with no edit destination, at which an issued revision may be exported.

viewer.description: Which viewer. `sequence`: the sequence, with its features and tracks along it. `structure`: a 3D structure, in Mol*. `alignment`: aligned sequences, a row each.

label.description: The tab's name. The viewer's own name if left out, such as Sequence.

sequence.description: The field it shows: a string with format `dna_sequence`, `rna_sequence` or `protein_sequence`.

features.description: A json field listing regions along it, as GenBank features are: each with a `type`, a `start` and `end` (from 1), and optionally a `name` and a `strand` (`forward`, `reverse` or `none`).

tracks.description: Json fields of values along it, one number per residue (or null where there's none), each drawn as a track under the residues, such as a hydropathy profile.

field.description: A json field whose schema is an array of numbers, or of numbers and nulls.

label.description: The track's name. The field's label if left out.

structure.description: The field it shows: a file field whose media types are chemical/x-mmcif or chemical/x-pdb, or both.

alignment.description: The field it shows: a file field of aligned FASTA, whose media types are chemical/seq-aa-fasta, chemical/seq-na-fasta or text/plain.

rows.description: A list of references to the sequences in Iki it aligns. A row whose FASTA header is one's HRID links to it; others, such as reads, are named by their headers.

reference.description: A reference to the sequence the others were aligned to, which the viewer shows first and can compare the others with.

label.description: What people's settings and the type's page call it, such as `A sample is in review`.

description.description: When it's sent and why, in a sentence, beside it in people's settings.

when.description: What sends it: a record being made (`created: true`), a field changing, optionally to or from some of its values, or for a request, its being sent to a service (`sent: true`) or one of its results released back (`released: true`).

sent.description: A request's: when it's sent to a service. It tells the service, by the lab roles its people hold there (`tell.roles`), and nobody of the project asking.

material.description: An immutable reference to material covered by the request. It may be empty only when the request specifies no physical material.

released.description: A request's: when one of its results is released back to the project that asked, whose people it tells.

field.description: The field whose change sends it: one of the record's own, or `ref.field`, a field of the record one of its references names, such as `instrument.service`.

to.description: For a state field, an enum or a yes-or-no field: only when it changes to one of these, such as a state it enters.

oneOf.description: A state, an enum's value, or true or false.

items.description: A state, an enum's value, or true or false.

from.description: For a state field, an enum or a yes-or-no field: only when it changes from one of these, such as a state it leaves.

oneOf.description: A state, an enum's value, or true or false.

items.description: A state, an enum's value, or true or false.

where.description: Only for records these conditions find, as the search API takes them: the type's fields compared with values, or with `{{ now }}` for a date or a time, such as bookings that haven't ended.

tell.description: Whom it tells. Each must be able to read the record when it's sent; whoever made the change isn't told unless `actor` says so, or an agent, a run or a trigger made it for them.

fields.description: The people these fields of the record name (`type: person`, or lists of them).

roles.description: Whoever holds one of these lab roles in the record's project, such as `qa`.

actor.description: Whoever made the change, even with their own hands.

message.description: What it says in Iki, written as a display title is: text with `{{ field or "text" }}` parts naming the record's fields or `hrid`. Emails never carry it: only what it is, the record's HRID and a link.

title.description: Its headline, such as `{{ hrid }} is ready for QA`. The record's HRID and the notification's label if left out.

body.description: A line or two under it.

email.description: Whether it's emailed to those who haven't chosen otherwise. Defaults to true.

required.description: Nobody can turn it off in Iki, for every project, one project, or one record; whether it's emailed stays their choice.
